description: When a user creates a cover letter from a saved job application, the letter is written by the AI from that offer and, when the application has a linked CV, from that CV. When the offer is no longer open, no letter is created and the user is told why.

userStories.title: A letter created from an application is written from the offer and the linked CV
userStories.description: As a user creating a cover letter from a saved job application, I want the letter written for me from the offer and my linked CV, so that I start from a real draft instead of an empty letter.
acceptanceCriteria: Submitting the creation form from an application stores a letter whose `opening_paragraph`, at least one `body_paragraphs` entry and `closing_paragraph` are non-empty AI text. Its `greeting` and `sign_off` are non-empty, in the letter's language. Its `company_name`, `job_title` and `job_application_id` match the application. Its `resume_id` is the CV selected in the form.
When a CV is selected, its content is used in the prompt: summary, experience and skills, as the existing route reads them. `sender_name` is the CV's contact name when that is non-empty.
When no CV is selected, the letter is generated from the offer alone and `resume_id` is null.

Language: The letter is written in the offer's language when it is detected as fr, en, de or it, otherwise in the page language. The same detection as the CV flow is used. A German offer opened under `/fr` gives a German letter.
When the application has no job description, the letter is generated from the job title, the company and the CV (if any). Creation is not refused for that reason.
If the AI fails or is rate-limited: a localized error is shown on the form; no letter is stored and the application's `cover_letter_id` is unchanged; the form stays filled so the user can retry.
The application's `cover_letter_id` points to the new letter, and the user lands in its editor showing the generated text.
While the letter is created, the submit button shows a localized busy label and is disabled. A double submit creates one letter.
Another user's application, or another user's CV id, is refused and nothing is created or linked.

FR-1: Creation from an application goes through one authenticated server route. That route reads the application and the CV with the user's session and explicit `user_id` checks. The client sends only identifiers and form fields (title, company, job title, selected CV id, locale). Offer and CV content is never trusted from the client.
FR-2: The availability check (US-002) runs before any AI call. It uses `safeFetch` with the existing job-board allowlist, a bounded timeout and a bounded redirect count. Only 404 and 410 mean closed.

FR-3: The AI prompt reuses `buildCoverLetterGenerationPrompt` and its JSON reply shape. The prompt states which language to write in, from the offer-language detection. The prompt's behaviour for the editor modal's existing calls is unchanged, which is pinned by test.

FR-4: Offer text, CV text and AI output are untrusted. AI output is sanitized as plain text before storage. Lengths and entry counts are bounded by the existing AI input limits. No raw AI reply or CV content is logged on the new path.

FR-5: The AI test stub is the guarded server-side stub from cv-from-job-complete, extended to the cover-letter generation. Its enabling conditions are unchanged. The availability fetch is stubbable for e2e under the same guard, so no e2e test reaches a real job board.
FR-6: No schema migration, no new dependency, no change to the host allowlist.
FR-7: New UI strings exist, non-empty, in fr, en, de and it (`src/locales/locale-parity.test.ts`).
Regression constraint: Creating a letter without an application stays exactly as today: client insert, the same default greeting and sign-off, no AI call, the `?resume_id=` pre-selection.
Regression constraint: The editor's generation modal and `POST /api/ai/generate-cover-letter` behave as before. Its existing prompt output is byte-identical, pinned by test.
Regression constraint: The three entry points keep their links and wording.
Regression constraint: Existing letters and applications are not modified, other than linking the new letter.

Regression constraint: The cover-letter editor, PDF export and the specs `e2e/cover-letter-editor-i18n.spec.ts`, `e2e/cover-letter-editor-spacing.spec.ts` and `e2e/cover-letter-pdf-export.spec.ts` stay green unchanged.
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline.

Verification: Unit tests: Route: ownership of the application and of the CV; deadline past, today, future and none; availability 404, 410, 200, 403, 5xx, timeout, host outside the allowlist, no URL; AI provider error, provider 429, our limit, unparsable reply → error and no insert; language from the offer with fallback; sanitized output; no description. Pre-selection: the application CV, `?resume_id=`, a foreign or missing id. The existing modal prompt unchanged, pinned.

Verification: e2e with the AI stub and a stubbed availability check, in fr and de: an application with a linked CV gives a generated letter in the offer's language, with "Lier à un CV" pre-selected and the stored row checked; an application without a CV gives a generated letter with no `resume_id`; a past deadline, and a 404 page, each show the message and create nothing; an AI failure shows the error and creates nothing; creating without an application is unchanged.
Verification: `security-review` on the new route, ownership, sanitization, the availability fetch (SSRF) and the stub guard.
Verification: `ui-expert` on the creation form (pre-selected CV, busy state, closed-offer message, error) and the resulting editor, in fr and de at 1440 and 375.
Verification: `code-reviewer`.
FAIL condition: A letter created from an open offer has an empty opening, body or closing.
FAIL condition: A letter is created, or linked, for an offer the check found closed (deadline past, or 404/410).
FAIL condition: An offer whose availability could not be determined is refused.
FAIL condition: A letter is created from another user's application or uses another user's CV.
FAIL condition: The availability check fetches a host outside the allowlist, or a private or internal address.
FAIL condition: "Lier à un CV" ignores the application's linked CV.
FAIL condition: Creation without an application, or the editor's generation modal, changes behaviour.
FAIL condition: An AI failure stores a letter.
BLOCKER condition: Detecting a closed offer reliably requires a schema change, a new dependency or widening the host allowlist. Report it; the owner decides.
BLOCKER condition: The AI cannot return the letter reliably within the current token budget and parsing. Report it with failure rates; the owner decides.
Out of scope: Creating a cover letter without a job application (`/cover-letters/new` without `jobApplicationId`, or with only `?resume_id=`). It stays exactly as today.
Out of scope: The editor's generation modal and `POST /api/ai/generate-cover-letter`: no behaviour change. The new path may reuse its prompt builder and parsing.
Out of scope: Cover-letter templates, editor layout, PDF/Word export.
Out of scope: Re-checking offers that already have letters; any periodic or background availability check; changing the application's status when the offer is closed.
Out of scope: Adding an "open/closed" column or any schema change.
Out of scope: Widening the job-board host allowlist.
Out of scope: Changing the AI provider, model or rate limits.
Out of scope: Job Search (`/dashboard/jobs`) cover-letter flows.

userStories.title: A closed offer creates no letter
userStories.description: As a user, I want to be told when the offer I am writing for is no longer open, so that I don't spend time on a letter for a closed position.
acceptanceCriteria: If the application's `deadline` is before today, submitting shows a localized message that the offer is no longer open. No letter is created and nothing is linked. "Today" is evaluated server-side, in UTC.

If the application's `job_url` is on an allowed job-board host and its page answers 404 or 410, the same message is shown and nothing is created. Redirects are followed and re-checked as `safeFetch` already does.
In every other case the letter is created as in US-001: no `job_url`; a host outside the allowlist; any other status (2xx, 3xx limit, 401/403, 429, 5xx); a timeout or network error.
The availability check runs server-side only, with a bounded time budget. The AI is not called when the offer is closed.
The message names the reason: deadline passed, or page no longer available.

userStories.title: "Lier à un CV" shows the application's CV
userStories.description: As a user whose application already has a linked CV, I want "Lier à un CV" to be set to that CV when I create the letter, so that the letter uses the right CV without my choosing it again.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening the creation form from an application whose `resume_id` is one of the user's CVs shows that CV selected in "Lier à un CV".
The user can still change or clear the selection, and the letter uses the final selection (US-001).
If the application has no linked CV, the select starts empty, unless `?resume_id=` names one of the user's CVs. In that case it starts on that CV, as today.
If the application's `resume_id` is not among the user's CVs, the select starts empty.
